key_idea: Build a hierarchy of correction-and-copy transforms using I-D=(I+E)(I-C). Each stage moves transition mass into rewards while keeping the number of active vertices under control. Every stage is estimated in one shared O(log n)-bit random environment, and enumerating all environments and taking the median gives the deterministic answer.
reason: The high-level skeleton is clear: a factorization identity moves probability into rewards, an integrated moment bound is paid for by enumeration, and a median turns the estimates into a decision. But nearly all of the weight sits in a long chain of technical pieces (rank channels, property-(T) mixing, compression into exception lists, adaptive fingerprints with a coupled induction, catalytic key comparison, and digit-by-digit space accounting). These verify more than they explain, so the reason the result holds is buried under bookkeeping.
